question: Assume today is 2026-09-01. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total value of online shopping transactions in South Korea in August 2026, in Korean won (KRW), as it will be first reported in the national statistics agency's monthly Online Shopping Trends release (온라인쇼핑동향, National Data Office, formerly Statistics Korea).

target.what: Total value of online shopping transactions (거래액) in South Korea during August 2026, as reported in the National Data Office (formerly Statistics Korea) monthly Online Shopping Trends (온라인쇼핑동향) release — the aggregate online shopping transaction value across all commodity groups and both mobile and
target.unit: KRW (current prices, total for the month)
target.publisher: National Data Office (국가데이터처, formerly Statistics Korea / 통계청) — Online Shopping Trends (온라인쇼핑동향)
target.caveats: Target period is completed relative to the 2026-09-01 cutoff but the official figure is not yet published (typically released ~1 month after month-end, so August 2026 data would appear around late September/early October 2026). Working interpretation: total online shopping transaction value (거래액), a

candidates.hypothesis: The target is a continuation of a monthly series; August 2026 value ≈ August 2025 value grown by the recent year-over-year trend, adjusted for August-specific seasonality (summer holiday, Chuseok timing — Chuseok falls in September/October, not August 2026). Own history gives the level and seasonal shape directly.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total online shopping transaction value (거래액) for all months 2023-01 through the latest published month before 2026-09-01 (ideally through 2026-07), plus the same-month prior-year values for August 2023, 2024, 2025. Minimum: August 2025 total and the 2026 monthly YoY growth rates published so far.
search_hints: Statistics Korea online shopping trends monthly transaction value 2025 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Online shopping is a large share of total retail sales; the target ≈ total retail sales value × online share. Retail sales index/value and the online share of retail (온라인 매출 비중) are published separately and can bridge to the target.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total retail sales value (소매판매액) for 2026 and the online/online-shopping share of retail sales (온라인쇼핑 비중) for recent months. Minimum: latest monthly retail sales value and the online share percentage.
search_hints: retail sales index Korea 2026 online share

candidates.hypothesis: Online transaction value can be cross-checked against card/electronic payment statistics and major platform GMV (Coupang, Naver Shopping, etc.). Platform GMV summed plus long-tail estimate approximates the total; payment statistics give an independent level check.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly card/electronic payment online transaction value (한국은행 지급결제통계 or 여신금융협회) for 2026; major platform GMV disclosures (Coupang Korea, Naver, Kakao, 11st) for Q2/Q3 2026. Minimum: one independent monthly online payment total or platform GMV aggregate.

candidates.hypothesis: Online shopping value ≈ parcel/online shipment volume × average order value. Parcel volume (택배 물동량) is a physical proxy; dividing by average transaction value per parcel gives the transaction value.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly parcel volume (택배 물동량) for 2026 from Korea Post / logistics associations, and average online order value (객단가) or average parcel value. Minimum: one monthly parcel volume figure and an average order value.

candidates.hypothesis: Published e-commerce market forecasts for Korea 2026 (e.g., from research firms, government plans) give an annual total that can be split by month using historical monthly shares, providing an independent level estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Korea e-commerce/online shopping market size forecast for 2026 (annual KRW), and historical monthly share of annual total (August share). Minimum: one 2026 annual forecast and an August monthly share.

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 has no Chuseok (falls later), but summer promotions, heat waves, and macro consumption trends (consumer sentiment, inflation) shift the level. Identifying measurable August-specific effects constrains the YoY adjustment in d1.
candidates.data_to_find: August 2026 consumer price inflation, consumer sentiment index, and any major platform promotion events (e.g., 8.8 sale, summer Black Friday) with reported GMV impact. Minimum: CPI YoY for August 2026 and one promotion-impact datapoint.

p1.role: June 2026 total online shopping transaction value (KRW)

methods.rationale: Anchors on the latest observed monthly total (June 2026, p1) and applies a wide seasonal/trend factor to reach August 2026. Dominant uncertainty is the month-to-month factor a1; the June anchor is well corroborated by p4/p5/p6.

p18.role: January 2026 parcel volume (parcels), used as a scale proxy for June 2026 monthly volume

a3.role: average online transaction value per parcel (KRW/parcel)

methods.rationale: Physical-flow route: parcel volume times average value per parcel. Uses January 2026 parcel volume (p18) as a monthly scale proxy (June 2026 volume ~580.75m is similar), scaled to August by a2 and converted to value by a3. Highly uncertain because a3 is derived from the same June data and parcel volume is only a partial proxy for online value (many online transactions are services/travel with no parcel).

p4.role: H1 2026 cumulative online shopping transaction value (KRW)

methods.rationale: Uses the H1 2026 cumulative total (p4) to derive an average monthly level (H1/6), then applies the same August/June factor a1. Provides a level check against m1 using a broader base; shares the a1 assumption so is not fully independent.

assumptions.name: August 2026 / June 2026 seasonal-and-trend factor
assumptions.rationale: No August 2026 or August 2025 monthly value is available; June 2026 is the latest observed month. August typically has no Chuseok and modest summer seasonality; online value has been growing ~10% YoY, so August 2026 is plausibly near June 2026 with a wide band reflecting unknown month-to-month seasonality and the CCSI softening (p40-p41).
assumptions.applies_when: Used to transfer the June 2026 observed total to August 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Historical monthly data showing a systematic August/June ratio outside 0.92-1.08, or evidence of a sharp August 2026 consumption shock.

assumptions.name: August 2026 / June 2026 parcel-volume ratio
assumptions.rationale: Parcel volumes are only observed through June 2026; August volume is assumed similar to June with a wide band reflecting summer seasonality and growth.
assumptions.applies_when: Used in the parcel-based route to scale June 2026 parcel volume to August 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Monthly parcel data for July/August 2026 showing a ratio outside 0.9-1.1.

assumptions.name: Average online transaction value per parcel
assumptions.rationale: June 2026 total (24,606.7 bn KRW) divided by June 2026 parcel volume (~580.75m) gives ~42,400 KRW per parcel; this is a derived bridge factor, not an independent observation, and is used to convert parcel volume to transaction value.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert August 2026 parcel volume into online transaction value.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that average order value per parcel differs materially from ~42,000 KRW in mid-2026.

assessment.note: Same June 2026 release: mobile value p2 and mobile share p3 are internally consistent with total p1 (p2/p1 ≈ 76.9%). One underlying source (National Data Office release reported by edaily), so not independent confirmation.
Quarterly and half-year totals are the same series aggregated; p5+p6 should equal p4 and p1 is the June component of p6. Same source, so this is internal consistency, not independent evidence.
August 2025 level, YoY increment and YoY rate are three renderings of one statistic (22.48tn = prior year + 1.39tn at 6.6%).

Monthly 2025 YoY growth rates from one article; they establish that 2025 growth accelerated in H2 (July 7.8%, Aug 6.6%) versus ~2% in H1, useful for judging whether the 2026 H1 ~10.7% rate is representative of August.

June 2026 (24.61tn, +10.7% YoY) versus August 2025 (22.48tn, +6.6% YoY): consistent with an accelerating 2026 trend; the June 2026 level implies June 2025 ≈ 22.23tn, close to the August 2025 level, so August 2026 should sit above June 2026 only via seasonality and continued growth.

Parcel volumes: monthly 2026 values sum to the H1 2026 cumulative; H1 growth 6.67% (2026) and 7.76% (2025) are consistent with the >6bn 2025 annual figure. Parcel volume grows slower than online transaction value, so value per parcel is rising — a conversion factor, not a direct substitute.
Per-capita figures are derived from the same parcel totals and population; they add no independent level information.

August 2026 CCSI 104.5, down 2.3p m/m but still above 100 and a smaller drop than April's -7.8p; sub-indices mostly fell 1-5p. Signals mildly softer August consumption but not a collapse — supports a modest downward adjustment to trend growth, not a level shift.

June 2026 commodity-group values (food 3.35tn, cosmetics 1.26tn, autos 1.19tn, telecom devices 0.89tn with +144% YoY) are components of the June total p1; they explain part of the elevated 10.7% growth (telecom device surge is a one-off that may not persist into August).
Online product share of retail rose 29.4%→30.0% Q1→Q2 2026; p7 (product-only H1) is a narrower scope than the target and cannot be substituted directly.
Cross-border flows are small relative to the total and are separate concepts (overseas direct sales/purchases), not components of domestic online shopping transaction value.

a1.role: August 2026 / August 2025 growth factor for total online shopping transaction value

methods.rationale: Direct seasonal-naive route: the August 2025 level grown by the recent YoY trend. This avoids the June 2026 anchor's telecom-device distortion (p39) and uses the same calendar month, so no June-to-August seasonal conversion is needed. Main failure mode: the 2026 YoY growth rate diverging from the ~10% observed through June.

p15.role: H1 2026 cumulative parcel volume (parcels), divided by 6 to give the average monthly parcel volume

a3.role: August 2026 / H1 2026 average monthly parcel-volume ratio

a2.role: average online transaction value per parcel (KRW/parcel)

methods.rationale: Physical-flow route: H1 2026 average monthly parcel volume (p15/6) adjusted to August by a3, times value per parcel (a2). Independent of the transaction-value series. Failure modes: online value includes food services and travel with few parcels, so a2 must absorb that gap; parcel volume grows slower than online value, so a2 embeds a rising trend.

assumptions.name: August 2026 / August 2025 growth factor for total online shopping transaction value
assumptions.rationale: June 2026 grew 10.7% YoY (p1) and H1 2026 averaged roughly 10%; 2025 growth accelerated into H2 (p58, p57: 7.8% July, 6.6% August 2025), so a base effect makes a repeat of ~9-10% plausible. August 2026 has no Chuseok (falls in September/October), same as August 2025, so no calendar distortion. The August CCSI decline (p40, p41) and weaker consumption-expenditure outlook (p46) tilt the factor slightly below the June rate; the June telecom surge (p39) is a June-specific distortion that does not carry into August because we anchor on August 2025. Centered at 1.09 with P10/P90 1.02-1.16.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 YoY growth trend of roughly 8-12% observed through June continues into August, and August 2026 has no major one-off demand shock.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp break in online growth (e.g., a July/August 2026 YoY rate below 5% or above 15%), or a major August 2026 platform event or regulatory shock.

assumptions.name: Average online transaction value per parcel (KRW/parcel)
assumptions.rationale: H1 2026 online value (p4, 145.7tn) divided by H1 2026 parcels (p15, 3.31bn) gives about 44,000 KRW per parcel. Because online value includes food services and travel that generate few parcels, the parcel-linked goods portion is somewhat lower per parcel, but high-ticket electronics and groceries push the average up; centered at the raw ratio with a wide range to absorb both effects.
assumptions.applies_when: Parcel volume is a stable proxy for the goods portion of online transactions and value-per-parcel is stable between H1 and August 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that value per parcel shifted sharply (e.g., a surge in high-ticket electronics or a collapse in low-value orders).

assumptions.name: August 2026 / H1 2026 average monthly parcel-volume ratio
assumptions.rationale: Monthly 2026 parcel volumes (p18-p21) vary within roughly ±8% around the H1 mean with no strong seasonal spike; August is a normal non-holiday month, so the August monthly volume should be close to the H1 average. Centered at 1.0.
assumptions.applies_when: August parcel volume behaves like other non-holiday months in 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Data showing August parcel volume systematically 10%+ above or below the H1 average.

methods.rationale: Direct seasonal-naive route: the August 2025 level grown by the recent YoY trend. kept.rationale: June 2026 grew 10.7% YoY (p1) and H1 2026 averaged roughly 10%; 2025 growth accelerated into H2 (p58, p57: 7.8% July, 6.6% August 2025), so a base effect makes a repeat of ~9-10% plausible. kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp break in online growth (e.g., a July/August 2026 YoY rate below 5% or above 15%), or a major August 2026 platform event or regulatory shock.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
